title: host on linux: disk IO saturated, everything stalls
scenario: On linux, a performance incident: disk IO saturated, everything stalls. Symptom: 'high %iowait, high await in iostat'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'io_saturation' for host on linux
expected_reasoning: High iowait points at storage, not CPU — measure per-device latency.
Attribute IO to a process (iotop/pidstat -d); understand the workload pattern.
Throttle the offender / fix the workload; escalate storage only if genuinely undersized.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'disk IO saturated, everything stalls' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('io_saturation') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Drop caches expecting it to fix IO (it doesn't).
Disable write barriers, risking data integrity on power loss.
hints: await + %util in iostat pinpoint the saturated device.
A backup/rebuild job is a common hidden IO source.
alternative_solution: Use ionice/blkio cgroup to deprioritize the batch job during business hours.
edge_cases: The saturation is a degraded RAID rebuilding, not a rogue process.
goal: Il sistema ha un problema di performance: disk IO saturated, everything stalls. Trova la causa e stabilizza il sistema.
